title: RAG pipeline step-through
description: Chunk a Cairnway FAQ, embed it, retrieve the closest chunks for a question and see a grounded answer next to a hallucinated one.
intro: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) lets a model answer from your own documents without retraining it. Walk through the six steps with the first question, then go back and try a chunk size of 8 sentences, a top K of 1, and the kayak question, which the FAQ can't answer.
takeaways: RAG has two phases. Ahead of time: split documents into chunks, turn each chunk into an embedding (a vector that captures its meaning) and store it in a vector database. For each question: embed the question, find the closest chunks, add them to the prompt, and generate.
Similar meaning means vectors that are close together. A similarity search finds the closest stored vectors; a normal keyword or key-value lookup can't.
Chunk size matters: chunks that are too big mix topics and add tokens, chunks that are too small lose the surrounding meaning.

Vector stores the exam names: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (with pgvector), and Amazon Neptune (Neptune Analytics). Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases runs the whole RAG pipeline for you.
RAG grounds answers in trusted text, which reduces hallucinations and makes answers citable and current. A Guardrails contextual grounding check can block answers that the source doesn't support.

store: Each chunk's vector is saved in a vector database together with the chunk's text, so the closest vectors can be found fast and their text handed to the model. This is a similarity search, also called a k-nearest-neighbour search.

The exam guide names these AWS options: Amazon OpenSearch Service (built-in vector search, also serverless), Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-compatible and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (both with the pgvector extension), and Amazon Neptune, whose Neptune Analytics stores vectors for GraphRAG.

Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases can run the whole pipeline: it chunks and embeds your documents, stores the vectors and retrieves them at question time. When a document changes, you re-ingest it and answers stay current without retraining the model.

questions.text: How long do I have to return a tent I haven't used?
questions.grounded: You can return unused gear within 30 days of delivery for a full refund.
questions.withoutRag: Most outdoor retailers give you 90 days, so you have 90 days to return your tent.

questions.text: The zipper on my tent broke. Can you fix it?
questions.grounded: Yes. Broken zippers on tents are repaired for free under the warranty.
questions.withoutRag: Zipper repairs cost $25 and take about two weeks.

questions.text: Can you deliver to the United Kingdom?
questions.grounded: No. Cairnway ships to the United States and Canada only.
questions.withoutRag: Yes, Cairnway ships worldwide, including the UK, in 7 to 10 days.

questions.text: Should I order my usual size in hiking boots?
questions.grounded: Cairnway's hiking boots run small, so order half a size up.
questions.withoutRag: Yes, our boots are true to size, so order your usual size.
